title: The Child Who Found the Error

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A child spots a mistake in the planting calendar: check it together, or trust the old count.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has been counting the days between full moons with pebbles, and says the planting calendar is wrong: it is a day off every year, and has been for a long time. (friend), the researcher who keeps the calendar, and another researcher got different answers when they checked. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject), (friend) and the other researcher count together for three moons, each with their own pebbles, and compare. (subject) is right. The calendar is fixed. (friend) makes (subject) the official pebble-keeper.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) thanks (subject) but keeps the old calendar. The next year, the rains come a week before planting time, by the calendar. (friend) looks at (subject)'s pebbles again, and goes very red.
